zh: 我们正在围绕 AI 打造这家公司,而这绝对是最好的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: So just don't overthink it and get in.
zh: 所以别想太多,进去就行。

speaker: Unknown
en: And honestly, I think that's been really a hallmark of how we've operated.
zh: 而且说实话,我认为这确实是我们运营方式的一个标志。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think...
zh: 我认为……

speaker: Unknown
en: Other firms can be, and not to throw any shade on anybody because I have such great respect, but, you know, you kind of get into these situations where we have to own 15 or 20% ownership or we don't do this and don't do that.
zh: 其他公司可能会,并不是要贬低任何人,因为我非常尊重他们,但是,你知道,你会陷入这样一种情况:我们必须拥有 15% 或 20% 的股权,否则我们就不做这个、不做那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the new Menlo that I'm part of has shown extreme flexibility to just do what makes sense.
zh: 而且我认为我所在的新 Menlo 展现了极大的灵活性,只做合理的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's get in this great company because once you're in, hey, if it takes off, there's plenty of opportunity to put more capital in.
zh: 我们进这家好公司吧,因为一旦进去了,嘿,如果它起飞了,有大量机会投入更多资本。

speaker: Unknown
en: So do we think that ownership today is less relevant than it ever used to be, given outcome scenarios being so much larger than they ever used to be?
zh: 那么我们是否认为,鉴于结果情景比以往大得多,股权占比今天比以往任何时候都更不重要了?

speaker: Unknown
en: By far.
zh: 明显是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, look, if you can get ownership, it's magical because if you own a lot and the company's worth a lot, that's going to be great, but...
zh: 我是说,你看,如果你能拿到股权,那很神奇,因为如果你拥有很多,而公司又值很多钱,那会非常棒,但是……

speaker: Unknown
en: A, there's a lot more capital coming in, so it's hard to even maintain that kind of ownership.
zh: 第一,有更多的资本进来,所以甚至很难维持那种股权占比。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we're in an outlier business right now, right?
zh: 但我们现在身处的是一个离群值的行业,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like I think for a long time, I mean, you know, I've been in the business for 25 years now.
zh: 就像,我认为很长一段时间,我是说,你知道,我入这行已经 25 年了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You were kind of saying like, hey, great outcomes are 300 million, 500 million, a billion.
zh: 大家会说,嘿,很棒的结果是 3 亿、5 亿、10 亿。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you're like, hey, you have to own 20% to get 100 million or whatever.
zh: 所以你就说,嘿,你得拥有 20% 才能拿到 1 亿或多少。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those are like, and I know you talk about it a lot on your show with Rory and Jason, all that.
zh: 那些就是,而且我知道你在你的节目里和 Rory 以及 Jason 聊过很多这些,诸如此类。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's not how the game is being played anymore.
zh: 这已经不是这个游戏的玩法了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like you have to be in the big outliers to drive great returns, and you're better off being in them at a very small percent than owning a large percent of a company that exits for three to 500.
zh: 就是你必须投中大的离群值才能驱动丰厚回报,而以很小的比例投中它们,好过拥有一个以 3 到 5 亿退出的公司的大比例。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those just aren't going to move the needle.
zh: 这些根本不会产生实质影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there a stage where price does matter for you?
zh: 对你们来说,有没有哪个阶段价格确实很重要?

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, you know, we announced our new funds, so we're pretty full stack.
zh: 嗯,你知道,我们宣布了新基金,所以我们基本上是全栈的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We can take big, concentrated positions.
zh: 我们可以持有大而集中的头寸。

speaker: Unknown
en: Fortunately, we've got LPs who like to co-invest with us.
zh: 幸运的是,我们有喜欢与我们联合投资的 LP。

speaker: Unknown
en: But, you know, we don't have a 10 or $20 billion fund, nor do we aspire to have that.
zh: 但是,你知道,我们没有一百亿或两百亿美元的基金,我们也不渴望拥有那样的基金。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's some quantum of capital that's like, hey, that's for somebody else, the next, next round.
zh: 所以存在某个资本量级,就像是,嘿,那是给别人的,是下一轮、再下一轮的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I don't know that it's as much of a...
zh: 但我不确定这是不是那么多是……

speaker: Unknown
en: Valuation thing, I think it's more because I would rather, you know, to be in the most amazing company, I would rather be in than not.
zh: 估值的问题,我认为更多是因为,你知道,对于最了不起的公司,我宁愿在里面,也不愿不在。

speaker: Unknown
en: Before we move to SPVs, new funds, you name it, I do have to ask, in terms of like levels of dilution, with the increased outcome scenarios and increased outcome sizes, do you think we're just normalizing an entirely new level of dilution that's inherent within these companies?
zh: 在我们转向 SPV、新基金等等之前,我确实得问一下,关于稀释程度,随着结果情景的增加和结果规模的增大,你认为我们是不是只是在将一种全新的、内在于这些公司的稀释水平常态化?

speaker: Unknown
en: Or is that exclusively for the frontier model companies?
zh: 还是说那只是前沿模型公司独有的?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's pretty rare, as you know, to find companies these days that don't end up raising a lot of capital way outside of the frontier companies and look anywhere in the AI stack, even the application companies.
zh: 我认为,正如你所知,如今要找到最终没有筹集大量资本的公司是相当罕见的——远远超出前沿公司之外,看看 AI 栈的任何地方,甚至应用公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, there's part of it that companies are growing faster than ever, so they want the capital to really be able to play offense.
zh: 我是说,其中一部分原因是公司增长得比以往任何时候都快,所以他们想要资本来真正能够打进攻。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's also kind of a part of this dynamic in the market right now where there's this signaling effect that every X months or a year, you know, you raise capital.
zh: 而且现在市场中这种动态还有一部分,就是存在这种信号效应,即每隔 X 个月或一年,你知道,你就融资一次。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's, you know, employees want to hear that to keep up with the labs and some of the retention.
zh: 就是,你知道,员工想听到这个,以便跟上实验室的步伐,还有一部分留人的考虑。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, you have to do more secondary.
zh: 你知道,你必须做更多的老股转让。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's just the landscape is just very, very different than what I grew up with.
zh: 所以这个格局就是非常、非常不同于我成长时所熟悉的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what I grew up with.
zh: 和我成长时所熟悉的(那种格局)。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're forgetting I have been doing this for 11 years now, my friend.
zh: 你忘了,我做这行已经 11 年了,我的朋友。

speaker: Unknown
en: I remember the days.
zh: 我记得那些日子。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know, it's terrifying.
zh: 我知道,很可怕。

speaker: Unknown
en: On the second round that you mentioned there, where you're like, okay, we really sized up.
zh: 关于你刚才提到的第二轮融资,你当时想,好吧,我们真的加大了规模。

speaker: Unknown
en: How did you think about that one?
zh: 你当时是怎么考虑那一轮的?

speaker: Unknown
en: And how did that come to be?
zh: 以及那是怎么促成的?

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, like if there was a playbook that I would love to repeat, it was this.
zh: 我是说,如果有一个我很乐意重复的打法,那就是这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, so we basically built a relationship, got into the company and said, look, we need to go all in Menlo style, you know, our recruiting team, our BD team, and just get close to the founding team, build relationships, see how we can have value.
zh: 我是说,我们基本上建立了关系,进入这家公司,然后说,听着,我们需要以 Menlo 式的方式全力以赴,你知道,我们的招聘团队、我们的 BD 团队,就是接近创始团队,建立关系,看看我们能如何提供价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's a lot of examples of that that we probably don't have time to go into, but we got to know them and we got to see them operate.
zh: 这样的例子很多,我们可能没时间一一展开,但我们逐渐了解他们,也看到了他们的运作方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's say that we in the round closed in something like March.
zh: 比如说,我们参与的这轮在大约三月完成交割。

speaker: Unknown
en: The model was launched in April.
zh: 模型在四月发布。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you start at zero and then sometime through the year, you'd see them adding 10 this month, eight the next.
zh: 所以你从零开始,然后这一年中的某个时候,你会看到他们这个月增加 10,下个月增加 8。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the revenue started to build.
zh: 所以收入开始积累起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: In parallel with that, you had Amazon and Google come in both with the big investments as well as technical partnerships around Bedrock, Vertex.
zh: 与此同时,Amazon 和 Google 进来了,既带来大额投资,也带来围绕 Bedrock、Vertex 的技术合作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then distribution relationships.
zh: 然后是分发关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you're like, okay, let's take a look from when we invested to now.
zh: 所以你就想,好吧,让我们看看从我们投资到现在。

speaker: Unknown
en: They've got a capital partner, a distribution partner, a technical partner, two of the biggest in the world.
zh: 他们有了资本伙伴、分发伙伴、技术伙伴,还是世界上最大的两家。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're alternative to OpenAI, who's kind of tied to one cloud with Azure.
zh: 他们是 OpenAI 的替代选择,而 OpenAI 有点被绑定在一家云上,即 Azure。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's like, hey, this is the multi-cloud provider.
zh: 所以就像是,嘿,这就是多云提供商。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you just saw this kind of revenue drumbeat start.
zh: 然后你就看到这种收入的鼓点开始敲响。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the seminal event was we held our LP meeting in November and we had an Anthropic executive named Nirav, who's kind of a jack of all trades at a very valuable one at Anthropic come and present.
zh: 但标志性的事件是,我们在十一月举行了 LP 会议,我们请了一位名叫 Nirav 的 Anthropic 高管来演讲,他在 Anthropic 算是个多面手,而且是非常有价值的一位。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he blew everyone away.
zh: 他让所有人都为之震撼。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like after the meeting, our LPs were like, this is crazy.
zh: 比如,会议结束后,我们的 LP 说,这太疯狂了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like this company is amazing.
zh: 这家公司太了不起了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even my partners were like, this is so amazing that we're in this company.
zh: 连我的合伙人都说,这太惊人了,我们投中了这家公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was just the description of like the power of the models.
zh: 就是那种对模型力量的描述。

speaker: Unknown
en: And how it was impacting so many applications already, human behavior, all that.
zh: 以及它已经如何影响着那么多应用、人类行为等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we had had a bunch of inbound leading up to that.
zh: 而且在那之前,我们已经收到了一大堆主动找上门来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we literally came out of that meeting and said, all right, we've got to do this.
zh: 所以我们几乎是开完那场会出来就说,好,我们必须干这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've got to figure out a way to lead the round.
zh: 我们得想办法领投这一轮。

speaker: Unknown
en: And two weeks later, we signed a term sheet.
zh: 两周后,我们签署了投资条款书。

speaker: Unknown
en: We aggregated all the demand from RLPs and folks we knew.
zh: 我们汇总了来自 RLP 和我们认识的人的所有需求。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, the rest is kind of history.
zh: 然后，你知道的，后来的事就大家都知道了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Are we in a new venture world of SPV usage?
zh: 我们是否正处于一个广泛使用 SPV 的全新风险投资世界？

speaker: Unknown
en: We do them for very late stage opportunities too.
zh: 我们在非常后期的机会中也会做 SPV。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you think about that and when to go aggressive on the SPV strategy and when it moves out of fund strategy?
zh: 你怎么看待这个问题，什么时候该在 SPV 策略上采取激进姿态，什么时候它就超出了基金策略的范畴？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I mean, I think it's really like what guardrails or kind of parameters have you set on your fund in terms of how much you want to put in a fund?
zh: 是的，我的意思是，我觉得这真的就是，就你想往一家基金里投多少钱而言，你在你的基金上设定了什么样的护栏或者说参数？

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you've got a billion dollar fund, you might say, hey, we only want $100 million max in a company.
zh: 所以如果你有一只十亿美元的基金，你可能会说，嘿，我们希望在任何一家公司最多只投 1 亿美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: But look, maybe we did 50 in the first round and we want to do 100 in the next round so we can't put it all in the main vehicle.
zh: 但你看，也许我们在第一轮投了 5000 万，下一轮想投 1 亿，这样我们就没法把全部都放进主载体里。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's do an SPV.
zh: 所以我们就做一个 SPV。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I don't think you have to do it.
zh: 所以我认为你不一定要这么做。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think oftentimes it's valuable to be able to do it because you can play offense if you need to write more capital to win a round.
zh: 我认为通常能够这样做是很有价值的，因为如果你需要写出更多资本才能赢下一轮，你就可以采取进攻姿态。

speaker: Unknown
en: And obviously it can be helpful to a company that you come with more strength.
zh: 而且显然，如果你带着更强的实力前来，这对公司是有帮助的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I mean, there's a side of it where you can say like, well, look, it's kind of extra economics at times to go outside your fund mandate and be more full stack and not let somebody else take it.
zh: 你知道，我的意思是，这方面你可以说，嗯，看，有时走出你的基金授权范围、做得更全栈、不让别人拿走这份份额，这算是一种额外的经济收益。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think for the most part for us, it's just like, let's kind of keep our fund size at a level that we think makes sense for the environment.
zh: 但我认为对我们来说，大多数情况下就是，让我们把基金规模保持在我们认为对当前环境合理的水平。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if a amount of capital per company goes outside that, then let's bring in our LPs.
zh: 而如果每家公司的投资金额超出了那个范围，那我们就把我们的 LP 引进来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Along the way, how do you think about...
zh: 在这一路上，你是怎么看待……

speaker: Unknown
en: When is the right time to take money off the table?
zh: 什么时候是把钱从桌上拿走的合适时机？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's tough because in this environment, the markups are happening so quickly.
zh: 这很难，因为在当前环境下，估值上调发生得太快了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, you're like, well, relative to when we invested, this multiple is amazing, but it's complicated, right?
zh: 你知道，你会想，嗯，相对于我们投资的时候，这个倍数太惊人了，但这很复杂，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like I think, A, if you're a believer, I think more than ever, we're in an environment where your outliers, your winners will compound.
zh: 比如我认为，第一，如果你是一个相信者，我认为我们比以往任何时候都更处于这样一个环境：你的异类、你的赢家会复利增长。

speaker: Unknown
en: And drive fund returns.
zh: 并驱动基金回报。

speaker: Unknown
en: So those are certainly not the ones you want to sell from.
zh: 所以那些肯定不是你想从中卖出的标的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now you can argue you might have some LPs, some, you know, if it's an older fund, some dynamics like that, where you want to give liquidity, but that would be like, maybe you take 10, 20% off the table.
zh: 当然你可以说你可能有一些 LP，一些，你知道的，如果这是一只较老的基金，会有一些这样的动态，你想要提供流动性，但那大概也就是你从桌上拿走 10%、20%。

speaker: Unknown
en: But for the most part, if we're in a winter, we want it to run.
zh: 但在大多数情况下，如果我们身处寒冬，我们希望它继续跑。

speaker: Unknown
en: We want to put in more capital.
zh: 我们想投入更多资本。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then at some point, you know, you feel like the company is maturing or maybe they're waiting a super long time to go public.
zh: 然后在某个时点，你知道的，你会觉得公司正在走向成熟，或者也许他们要等非常长的时间才能上市。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you'd like to say, take some chips off the table, but it's not something we spent a lot of time on.
zh: 而你会想说，收走一些筹码，但这不是我们花很多时间去考虑的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: When was the most nervous time along the last 18 months for you as an Anthropic shareholder?
zh: 作为 Anthropic 的股东，在过去 18 个月里你最紧张的时刻是什么时候？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's amazing today.
zh: 今天真是太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a great state of play today.
zh: 今天的状态非常好。

speaker: Unknown
en: When were you like... Maybe I'll go back even, I'll expand your window to 24 months.
zh: 你什么时候觉得……也许我再把时间往回推，我把你的窗口扩大到 24 个月。

speaker: Unknown
en: When we did the SPV, Anthropic wasn't a household name yet.
zh: 当我们做那个 SPV 的时候，Anthropic 还不是家喻户晓的名字。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like we saw everything going on and like how amazing this company was.
zh: 我们看到了发生的一切，看到了这家公司有多惊人。

speaker: Unknown
en: But from the outside, it wasn't quite as obvious.
zh: 但从外部来看，这并不那么明显。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you know, even to get, you know, the whole syndicate that we pulled together and I had to give my friend Ravi and...
zh: 所以，你知道，就连要把我们拉起来的整个辛迪加凑齐，我还得给我的朋友 Ravi 和……

speaker: Unknown
en: Byron a call to bring them into the round as well, which all worked out.
zh: Byron 打个电话，把他们也叫进这一轮，这一切最终都成了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it wasn't, it was just, that was very nerve wracking because Menlo had never done an SPV before.
zh: 但这不是……那真的是非常让人神经紧绷，因为 Menlo 之前从未做过 SPV。

speaker: Unknown
en: This was your first SPV?
zh: 这是你们的第一个 SPV 吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: This happened to be over 500 million.
zh: 这一次碰巧超过了 5 亿。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you can imagine like, and by the way, it gives me great empathy for entrepreneurs, which I have anyway, because I understand how hard this is.
zh: 所以你可以想象，顺便说一句，这让我对创业者产生了极大的同理心，虽然我本来就有，因为我理解这有多难。

speaker: Unknown
en: But like being on the front lines, having to be the person kind of, you know, capital raising, talking to these investors, getting an occasional turndown.
zh: 但就像站在第一线，不得不成为那个，你知道的，做资本募集的人，和这些投资人交谈，偶尔遭到拒绝。

speaker: Unknown
en: Having to answer second and third order questions, sometimes annoying, no offense to anybody.
zh: 不得不回答二阶三阶的问题，有时挺烦人的，无意冒犯任何人。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's tough, man.
zh: 那真的很难，兄弟。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's really tough.
zh: 那真的非常难。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that was my most nerve wracking, but at the same time coming out the other side of it, the most exhilarating and obviously all that work was very worth it.
zh: 所以那是我最紧张的时刻，但同时，从另一头走出来之后，又是最令人振奋的，而且显然所有那些工作都非常值得。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll run through a couple other, the deep seek moment.
zh: 我再快速过另外几个，deep seek 时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, that was like, oh my God, what's happened?
zh: 你知道，那就像，天哪，发生了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And now you can't even remember that.
zh: 而现在你甚至都想不起来那事了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then there was the, the Dow moment.
zh: 然后还有那个，Dow 时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you know, it's just like this environment is so dynamic, right?
zh: 你知道的，就是这个环境实在太动态了，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like everything's moving so quickly that there's just like a new challenge and opportunity, both crisis and opportunity, seemingly every six months or so.
zh: 就是一切都移动得太快，以至于似乎每六个月左右就有一个新的挑战和机遇，既是危机也是机遇。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a weird thing.
zh: 这是个奇怪的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Mark Andreessen says he often ventures about the VC firm lending their brand to legitimize the company.

speaker: Unknown
en: Anthropic.

en: It has been incredible for Menlo and for you, and it's been a massive brand builder in AI, positioning you as one of the leading firms.

en: Another that you've done is Lovable.

en: I think we intercepted them around, well, we kind of tried to get in when they were around 30, 30 of error, but around we did was around 150.

speaker: Unknown
en: So you're kind of looking at...

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a phenomenon.
zh: 这是一种现象。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's numbers and then there's the market and then there's the founder, right?
zh: 所以有数字，然后有市场，然后有创始人，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So the numbers were just like ripping and you're like, all right, so this company is going to go from zero to 300 in a year.
zh: 所以当时数字就是在狂飙，你就想，好吧，这家公司一年内会从零做到 3 亿。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even if you assume it decelerates to whatever, a three X growth rate, that's 300 to a billion.

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm talking about when we first made the investment.

speaker: Unknown
en: And then, you know, you compound out from there and you're like.

zh: 当然，在我风投生涯的前，比方说 23 年里，你从没见过任何类似的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now there's a few more examples, but clearly this was an outlier, even amongst outliers.
zh: 现在多了几个例子，但很显然，即使在离群值之中，这也是一个离群值。

en: I think the thing that we also really gravitated to here, aside from like Anton, he's very visionary.
zh: 我认为我们在这里也真正被吸引的一点，除了比如 Anton——他非常有远见。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's kind of the voice of the category.

speaker: Unknown
en: I think he's got some very unique and distinctive plans about why this kind of 99% of people, as they like to call it, everybody who was never a coder.

speaker: Unknown
en: and programmer but making everyone become creators so you had like this massive vision we felt like an iconic entrepreneur and then like crazy numbers that you could do whatever model you wanted and you're like look if this thing keeps compounding and this is really the company that we believe this will be one of the most valuable companies of all time.
zh: 和程序员，但让每个人都成为创作者，所以你就有这种巨大的愿景，我们感觉是一位标志性的企业家，然后还有疯狂的数字，你可以用任何你想要的模型，你就会想，看，如果这个东西持续复利增长，而这真的是我们所相信的那家公司，这将会成为有史以来最有价值的公司之一。

en: Do margins matter anymore?

en: They do a lot.

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, we're in this kind of like tricky period as investors where right now a lot of great companies have low margins, 20 to 30 percent margins.
zh: 而且，你知道，作为投资者，我们正处于这种有点棘手的时期，现在很多很棒的公司利润率很低，20 到 30% 的利润率。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, they all probably have a path to get to 60 or 70.
zh: 而且，你知道，它们可能都有一条路可以走到 60 或 70。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, a lot of companies, just because of the cost of computing inference, it's harder to say you're going to be an 80, 90% gross margin company anymore.
zh: 你知道，很多公司，仅仅因为推理计算的成本，已经很难说你会成为一家 80%、90% 毛利率的公司了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But, you know, great companies are, you know, 60, 70% gross margin.
zh: 但是，你知道，伟大的公司是，你知道，60%、70% 的毛利率。

speaker: Unknown
en: But, you know, the path to get there is like, hey, I'm going to do some optimizations.
zh: 但是，你知道，到达那里的路径就像是，嘿，我要做一些优化。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not completely tied to inference around, you know, my cost structure.
zh: 我不会完全绑死在推理上，你知道，就我的成本结构而言。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm probably going to do something complementary to the leading labs with my own data and build a model that kind of gets my gross margin up.
zh: 而且我可能会用我自己的数据做一些与领先实验室互补的事情，构建一个能把我的毛利率提上去的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you're intercepting a lot of these hypergrowth companies with margins that are atypical for what we usually invest in.
zh: 所以你正在大量碰到这些超高速增长的公司，它们的利润率对于我们通常投资的对象来说是不典型的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you're trying to figure out which ones actually have a credible plan to get to a great margin structure.
zh: 而且你在试图弄清楚哪些公司真的有一个可信的计划能达到一个很好的利润率结构。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for what it's worth, I think Lovable is one of those.
zh: 顺便说一句，我认为 Lovable 就是其中之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: The margin structure of Lovable will be changed greatly with the utilization of open source, which is obviously much cheaper.
zh: Lovable 的利润率结构将随着开源的利用而发生巨大变化，开源显然要便宜得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: That goes against one of the other investments being Anthropic.
zh: 这与你们的另一项投资 Anthropic 相抵触。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you see them as like hedges against each other?
zh: 你把它们看作彼此的对冲吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you worry about the progression of open source given how much can be done now with open source?
zh: 鉴于现在用开源能做这么多事情，你担心开源的进展吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm intrigued how you think about that.
zh: 我很好奇你是怎么考虑这个问题的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

en: I mean, first of all, Anthropic is a fantastic partner to Lovable and vice versa, but like this market is so big.
zh: 我是说，首先，Anthropic 是 Lovable 的绝佳合作伙伴，反之亦然，但是这个市场太大了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's really two dimensions to that.
zh: 所以这其实有两个维度。

speaker: Unknown
en: One, some people worry about Lovable and Anthropic tripping over each other.
zh: 第一，有些人担心 Lovable 和 Anthropic 会互相绊倒。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think Anthropic always comes to things a little more like the technical user and Lovable comes at it more from the lay user.
zh: 我认为 Anthropic 总是以更偏向技术用户的方式来对待事情，而 Lovable 更多是从普通用户的角度出发。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm sure there's probably some overlap in the middle, but I think there's plenty of big space for each one to do extremely well.
zh: 我确信中间可能有一些重叠，但我认为有足够大的空间让每一方都做得极其出色。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, look.
zh: 而且，你知道，你看。

speaker: Unknown
en: Cursor was about as in the crosshairs of Anthropic as possible, and I think they still had a pretty darn good outcome.
zh: Cursor 曾几乎是处在 Anthropic 的十字准星正中，我认为他们仍然取得了相当不错的结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the whole open source topic, look, it's like any market.
zh: 但整个开源的话题，你看，它就像任何市场一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you start off in a certain way, it's just like, look, I want to get something running.
zh: 当你以某种方式起步时，就像是，看，我想让某个东西先跑起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to get it out there and just prove I've got a cool product.
zh: 我想把它推出去，证明我有一个很酷的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you just default to the simplest thing.

speaker: Unknown
en: Over time, you do more optimizations, right?

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, that's kind of like the North Star there is like, hey, you would have some intelligent layer that intercepts an API call from any application and basically says, what's the best model for me?
zh: 而且，你知道，那里的北极星差不多就是，嘿，你会有一层智能层，它拦截来自任何应用程序的 API 调用，基本上是在说，对我来说最好的模型是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like across whatever efficiency frontier I'm trying to optimize for.
zh: 就是在我想要优化的任何效率前沿上。

en: Is it price?

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it reasoning?
zh: 是推理吗？

en: Or is it performance?
zh: 还是性能？

en: You know, latency, things like that.
zh: 你知道，延迟，诸如此类的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's scale, like that's the kind of stuff you need as a company to manage and optimize your business.
zh: 而且这是规模化，就像是，作为一家公司，你需要这类东西来管理和优化你的业务。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so wave one of AI is like, let's just get it going.
zh: 所以 AI 的第一波就像是，让我们先把它跑起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Wave two is like, let's get a lot more sophisticated about what we use and when and how.
zh: 第二波就像是，让我们对用什么、什么时候用、怎么用变得更加精细。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're getting sophisticated about what you use when and how cost optimization comes into it.
zh: 如果你在对用什么、什么时候用、怎么用变得更精细，成本优化就进来了。

en: So I do just wonder like if open source can do 96% of enterprise workflows, does that not dramatically reduce the TAM of frontier model companies?

speaker: Unknown
en: And maybe we're so early that it's still $10 trillion for a TAM, but like maybe Anthropic and OpenAI solve cancer and climate change and your email tagging is done by open source.

speaker: Unknown
en: Is that how you think?
zh: 你是这么想的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: No, I think the foundation models, let's say specifically Anthropic, have such special models, performant, intelligent models.
zh: 不，我认为基础模型，比如说具体地 Anthropic，拥有如此特别的模型，高性能的、智能的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: This can be hard for somebody to just kind of say, I've used open source with my data.

speaker: Unknown
en: It's going to be functional and positive for some amount of what you're doing, but I just don't think it can be powerful enough to really, you know, displace it.

speaker: Unknown
en: My mindset generally would be like you're going to use multiple models.

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think it goes to that.
zh: 我不认为会走到那一步。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, you were talking more cost, but I don't think it goes to that 96% because what's happening is companies see this like, yes, I can get lower cost, but if I use Anthropic.
zh: 嗯，你刚才更多谈的是成本，但我不认为会走到那个 96%，因为现在发生的情况是公司看到这一点，就像，是的，我可以获得更低的成本，但如果我用 Anthropic。

speaker: Unknown
en: It actually increases my customer retention.
zh: 它实际上提高了我的客户留存率。

speaker: Unknown
en: I generate more revenue.
zh: 我产生更多收入。

speaker: Unknown
en: I get users to engage with the platform more.
zh: 我让用户更多地与平台互动。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that is what the data is suggesting now with a lot of application companies.
zh: 而这正是如今数据在很多应用公司身上所显示的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there's certain API calls that just don't need that level of functionality.
zh: 但有些 API 调用确实不需要那种程度的功能。

speaker: Unknown
en: And frankly, it's good for everybody.
zh: 而且坦白说,这对所有人都有好处。

en: It keeps Anthropic on their toes to keep innovating.
zh: 它让 Anthropic 保持警觉,持续创新。

speaker: Unknown
en: Most innovative company around, so they'll keep innovating, not stay still.
zh: 它是当今最具创新力的公司,所以他们还会继续创新,不会停滞不前。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then startups innovate in their own way with open source.
zh: 然后初创公司则用开源以自己的方式创新。

en: Do you think the costs have to come down for AI?

speaker: Unknown
en: Does AI have to get significantly cheaper and will we see this cost curve come down massively?
zh: AI 必须变得显著更便宜吗?我们会看到这条成本曲线大幅下降吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, I mean, I think it's like any product, you know, that you can argue that the cheaper it is, the more it kind of opens up the market because you can do more for less than that.
zh: 嗯,我觉得这就像任何产品一样,你可以说它越便宜,就越能打开市场,因为你用更少的成本能做更多的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, those economic curves always spark activity.
zh: 你知道,这种经济曲线总是会激发出活动。

speaker: Unknown
en: But, you know, I mean, look, even within the Anthropic family, right?
zh: 但是,你看,即使在 Anthropic 家族内部,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like you've got Sonnet, you've got Opus, you've got Fable.
zh: 比如你有 Sonnet,有 Opus,有 Fable。

speaker: Unknown
en: So even Anthropic itself is innovating around, you know, hey, it's not one size fits all.
zh: 所以就连 Anthropic 自己也在围绕这一点创新,就是,嘿,这不是一刀切的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think you're going to have the combination of something like that, a family of models from Anthropic, and then a set of open source models and things that you train with your own data.
zh: 所以我认为你会有这样的组合:来自 Anthropic 的一系列模型,再加上一套开源模型,以及用你自己的数据训练的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you're going to look across that whole tapestry and say, hey, I'm using 50% this, 30% that, 20% this.
zh: 然后你会纵观这整幅图景,说,嘿,我 50% 用这个,30% 用那个,20% 用这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And those are the kind of optimizations that happen at scale.
zh: 而这些就是在大规模下才会发生的那类优化。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's the stage of market that I think we're just...
zh: 而那就是我认为我们刚刚……

speaker: Unknown
en: entering into, which makes it a lot more fascinating, frankly, because there's going to be so many kind of second and third order companies that spike and take off versus the whole market being concentrated.

zh: 我非常天真,所以有些事情我不理解,比如我们看到,显然,OpenAI 有 Jalapeno,据报道 Anthropic 正在与三星合作打造自己的芯片,DeepSeeker 在打造自己的芯片,Meta 在打造自己的芯片。

en: Do you have to be full stack today, do you think?

zh: 这是不是我们看到所有人都进入芯片层的原因?

en: The biggest death knell always for me is like when it's like, oh, I worked with Matt on my previous company for seven years and I'm like, okay, I'm done.
zh: 对我来说,最大的丧钟永远是这种时候:哦,我上一家公司和 Matt 共事了七年——我就想:好了,我放弃。

speaker: Unknown
en: And relationships mean so much in this business because it is high trust matters so much and both within a venture firm and with the companies we work with.
zh: 在这个行业里,关系意味着太多,因为这是高信任的行业,信任太重要了——无论是在风投机构内部,还是在我们合作的公司那边。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's hard to establish that in some shotgun wedding, some sprints.
zh: 所以很难在一次闪婚式的仓促结合、一场冲刺中建立起这种东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we try to be very intentional about getting out ahead of things.
zh: 所以我们非常刻意地试图走在事情的前面。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I'd say for the best companies, they're always going to be this like kind of jump ball and it's incredibly important to know someone who's associated with the company who can kind of help guide you in, land the plane a little bit.
zh: 你知道,我想说,对于最好的公司来说,它们永远都会像是一种"争球"的局面,而认识一个与这家公司有关联、能帮你引路进来、帮飞机平稳落地一点的人,至关重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you don't have that and another investor does, like, hey, this person has worked with this board member for 10 years and they had a great experience in some big outcome.
zh: 而如果你没有这种关系,另一个投资人却有——比如,嘿,这个人和这位董事会成员共事了 10 年,他们有过很棒的合作经历,还拿到过一次很大的成果。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, it's more things like that.
zh: 你知道,更多是类似这样的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's rarely just like straight up, you know, valuation, stuff like that.
zh: 很少会单纯就是,你知道的,估值之类的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, valuation can be painful, but for the right companies, you know, you do what it takes to be in.
zh: 是的,估值可能很痛苦,但对于合适的公司,你知道,你会不惜代价进场。

speaker: Unknown
en: The single biggest mistake for me is always actually focused around ownership.
zh: 对我来说,最大的一个错误其实总是围绕持股比例。

speaker: Unknown
en: There have been several companies where we've had like 1% offered to us, Steel, Eleven Labs, StarCloud, where we were like, 1%, we can't be doing that.
zh: 有好几家公司,对方只给我们 1% 左右——Steel、Eleven Labs、StarCloud——我们当时想:1%?这我们不能干。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now I look back and all of them would have returned huge amounts of money.
zh: 现在回头看,这些公司本来全都会带来巨额回报。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the way I was trained and I learned that for most of my career, so it took me a lot to kind of shed that.
zh: 我就是那样被训练出来的,职业生涯大部分时间学的都是那一套,所以我花了很大力气才摆脱掉它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you think LPs understand that?
zh: 你觉得 LP 们理解这一点吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Because LP is always like high ownership portfolio, you know, constrained portfolio sizes, concentration, benchmark.
zh: 因为 LP 永远都是那一套:高持股比例的组合,你知道,受限制的组合规模、集中投资、benchmark。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you think they get that the game has changed?
zh: 你觉得他们明白游戏已经变了吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think they see the results, right?
zh: 我认为他们看到的是结果,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: So like maybe not upfront, but we're pretty explicit with them that we kind of have like, hey, here's a core position in a fund.
zh: 所以也许不是预先就知道,但我们跟他们说得很明确,我们大致是这样一个结构:嘿,这是基金里的一个核心仓位。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then here we call like tracker checks or starter checks.
zh: 然后还有这些,我们称之为 tracker check 或 starter check。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or frankly, even look at our Anthology Fund, right?
zh: 或者坦白说,看看我们的 Anthology Fund,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like that's over 50 companies, somewhere between 100K and 1 million where you kind of get in a seed round.
zh: 就是那个投了 50 多家公司的基金,金额在 10 万到 100 万之间,差不多是在种子轮进去的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the companies that have graduated out of that have been Open Router, Whisper, Axiom Math.
zh: 而从那里毕业出来的公司有 Open Router、Whisper、Axiom Math。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's a couple of things.
zh: 所以这里面有几个要点。

speaker: Unknown
en: One that gives us a bit of proprietary, quote, deal flow, but it gives you the opportunity to be in the cap table, get to know the entrepreneur.
zh: 一是它给了我们一点点所谓的"独家"项目来源,但它也让你有机会进入股权结构表、去认识创业者。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then pounce when you see something's working.
zh: 然后当你看到有什么东西跑起来了,就猛扑上去。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I would say if you get even a wedge into a company, you're 10x more likely to be able to participate significantly in the next round or lead.
zh: 我想说的是,只要你哪怕在一家公司里拿到一个小小的立足点,你能在大额参与下一轮或领投的可能性就会高 10 倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think LPs get that or they are getting it.
zh: 我认为 LP 们懂这一点,或者说他们正在懂。

speaker: Unknown
en: I totally agree with you.
zh: 我完全同意你。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you do those checks so you can concentrate capital more with the progression of the company.
zh: 而你之所以做那些支票,是为了随着公司的推进能更集中地投入资本。

speaker: Unknown
en: I went viral on BC Braggs.
zh: 我在 BC Braggs 上走红了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Matt, when you did our last show, I was very amenable and sweet and nice little kind of Harry Potter adventure.
zh: Matt,你上次上我们的节目时,我非常随和、亲切,像是一场美好可爱的小小哈利·波特式冒险。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now,
zh: 现在,

speaker: Unknown
en: They're quite binary.
zh: 它们相当二元。

speaker: Unknown
en: And apparently a lot of people don't always like what I say.
zh: 而且显然,很多人并不总是喜欢我说的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: And VC Braggs in particular took real problem with me because I said, basically, I turned down a company the other day because they were going from like one and a half to five to 15.
zh: 尤其是 VC Braggs 对我特别有意见,因为我说了,大意是,前几天我拒绝了一家公司,因为他们要从大概 1.5 到 5 再到 15。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's an opportunity cost of capital.
zh: 而资本是有机会成本的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's very real.
zh: 所以这是非常真实的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the growth expectations are just very different.
zh: 而且增长预期就是非常不一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: In other words, triple, triple, double, double.
zh: 换句话说,三倍、三倍、两倍、两倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just not exciting enough anymore.
zh: 它已经不够令人兴奋了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I got chastised for this.
zh: 所以我因此受到了责备。

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you with me that fundamentally, if I bring you a 1 to 5 and then a 5 to 15, again, it's great, I'm not belittling it, but that's just not the venture game today.
zh: 你同意我吗，从根本上说，如果我给你一个 1 到 5,然后再一个 5 到 15,再说一次，这很棒，我不是在贬低它，但这已经不是今天的风投游戏了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not.
zh: 不是。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not.
zh: 不是。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's hard to say and it's hard to change, you know, the context, the 20 plus years of context around what good and great was.
zh: 而这很难说出口，也很难改变，你知道的，那种语境，关于什么是好、什么是伟大的 20 多年的语境。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that's the reality.
zh: 但这就是现实。

speaker: Unknown
en: The environment has changed.
zh: 环境已经变了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you look around and you're like, well, that used to be top 5%, and now it looks more like top 50%, well, we're not trying to be in top 50%, right?
zh: 所以如果你环顾四周，你会想，嗯，那过去是前 5%,现在看起来更像前 50%,嗯，我们并不是想进入前 50%,对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's just the reality.
zh: 所以这就是现实。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, it's not controllable by us as investors when we look around and see these companies doing zero to 100 in a year, never seen anything like it.
zh: 我是说，当我们环顾四周，看到这些公司在一年内从零做到 100 时，这不是作为投资者的我们能控制的，从未见过这样的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's more examples of that than I can probably count right now.
zh: 而这样的例子多得我现在可能都数不过来。

speaker: Unknown
en: What company are you not in that you would most like to be in?
zh: 哪家公司你没有在里面，却最希望自己能在里面？

speaker: Unknown
en: There are several.
zh: 有好几家。

speaker: Unknown
en: One company that I've really admired and as the kind of like outlier entrepreneurs, in my history going back, like you look at the companies that became great, you know, when I was early days at Clander, it was like, you know, Jeff Bezos and later on Danielak and the Collison brothers and like somehow or another, these amazing founders end up manifesting the company.
zh: 有一家我真正钦佩的公司，作为那种异类企业家，回溯我的经历，你看那些变得伟大的公司，你知道，当我在 Clander 的早期时，是，你知道，Jeff Bezos,后来是 Danielak 和 Collison 兄弟，然后不知怎的，这些了不起的创始人最终成就了这家公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't necessarily think it was that they chose the right market or I mean, somewhat they did.
zh: 我不一定认为是因为他们选对了市场，我是说，某种程度上他们确实选对了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it was really just the force of nature, the creativity, the vision, the execution, their ability to raise capital, hire the best talent, all that.
zh: 但真正的原因是那种自然之力，创造力，愿景，执行力，他们融资的能力，招到最优秀人才的能力，所有这些。

speaker: Unknown
en: So anyway, I think an example of that in Europe, just because it's close to home for you, would be someone like Matty at Eleven Labs.
zh: 所以总之，我认为欧洲的一个这样的例子——就因为它是你的家门口——会是像 Eleven Labs 的 Matty 这样的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Very big respect for him.
zh: 对他非常尊重。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you know, I don't want to give everyone on the podcast my whole pipeline, but just because that's one you know well, I'll throw that out there.
zh: 所以，你知道，我不想在这个播客上把我的整个项目储备都告诉大家，但正因为那是你很熟悉的一家，我就把它说出来吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: What was the most controversial deal inside Manlo that you remember?
zh: 你还记得的 Manlo 内部最有争议的交易是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: The obvious answer is Anthropic in some ways, but I'm trying to think about, and by the way, there was two controversial points around that.
zh: 显而易见的答案在某种程度上是 Anthropic,但我在努力回想，顺便说一句，围绕它有两个有争议的点。

speaker: Unknown
en: One was, you know, the first just like, is this really what a venture fund does?
zh: 一个是，你知道，首先就是，这真的是风投基金该做的事吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And the second was like...
zh: 第二个是……

speaker: Unknown
en: We've never done an SPV before.
zh: 我们以前从未做过 SPV。

speaker: Unknown
en: Are we really going to go down this path?
zh: 我们真的要走这条路吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I can't really remember offhand anything that was that profound and felt like, wow, we're kind of putting the reputation of the firm, especially the bigger SPV, on the line to kind of pull this off and breaking new ground.
zh: 我一时想不起还有什么事那么重大，让人感觉，哇，我们某种程度上是在拿公司的声誉——尤其是那个更大的 SPV——冒险，来把这事儿办成，并且开辟新天地。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the great thing about our partners, we've got a very technical group.
zh: 我认为我们合伙人的好处在于，我们是一个非常技术型的团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're small enough to have high alignment.
zh: 我们足够小，因此能保持高度一致。

speaker: Unknown
en: We respect each other a lot.
zh: 我们非常尊重彼此。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's easy to make, you know, we listen to each other, make a decision.
zh: 做起来很容易，你知道，我们倾听彼此，做出决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I don't find things that controversial.
zh: 所以我不觉得事情那么有争议。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't really ascribe to this point of view where you need like a bunch of no's and there's one person who's a yes and that leads to an outlier.
zh: 我并不真正认同这种观点：你需要一堆说「不」的，然后有一个说「是」的人，而这最终造就一个异类。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know there are examples of that, but that's not really been my experience in the firms I've been part of or with our team.
zh: 我知道有那样的例子，但在我曾参与的公司里，或者在我们的团队里，那并不是我真正的经历。

speaker: Unknown
en: Final one before we move into a quickfire.
zh: 在进入快问快答之前的最后一个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I am not great at maths, but if I do like a little bit of a back of a napkin on Anthropic and distributions, it'll distribute around $10 billion in carry.
zh: 我数学不好，但如果我就 Anthropic 和分配在餐巾纸背面粗略算一下，它会分出大约 100 亿美元的 carry。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's quite a lot of monopoly money, Matt.
zh: 这可是相当多的大富翁游戏币，Matt。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not in Cary, right?
zh: 不是在 Cary,对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Our position is north of that.
zh: 我们所持的份额超过那个数。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can do the math on what Cary usually is.
zh: 你可以算算 Cary 通常是多少。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's not quite that on Cary, but yeah.
zh: 所以在 Cary 上不完全是那个数，不过，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Totally understand.
zh: 完全理解。

speaker: Unknown
en: Two to three billion.

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a very big number.
zh: 这是一个非常大的数字。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you think about firm sustenance when there is such a big win?
zh: 当出现这么大的胜利时，你如何看待机构的存续？

speaker: Unknown
en: We have seen firms candidly struggle to maintain dominance when everyone makes so much money, bluntly.
zh: 我们见过，坦率地说，一些机构在每个人都赚那么多钱时艰难地维持主导地位，直白地说。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you think about sustenance post such success?
zh: 在这样的成功之后，你怎么考虑存续问题？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think Menlo has always had a challenger mentality since myself and Venki came over a little over 10 years ago and kind of Sean Carrollin came back and Mark Siegel was the partner who was there who kind of put the band together.
zh: 我认为 Menlo 一直有一种挑战者心态，自从我和 Venki 在 10 年多前过来，还有 Sean Carrollin 差不多那时候回来，Mark Siegel 是当时在那里的合伙人，差不多就是把乐队组建起来的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And ever since that moment about 11 years ago, it's just been a grind, a fight, a build exhilarating to kind of get to this point.
zh: 而从大约 11 年前的那个时刻起，就一直是苦干、一场战斗、一番建设，令人振奋，才走到今天这一步。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I feel like everyone we've brought along has kind of felt Menlo
zh: 而且我觉得我们一路带进来的每个人都多少感受到了 Menlo

speaker: Unknown
en: Move up that stack and be more and more successful.
zh: 沿着那个栈往上走，变得越来越成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think what's driving us is what you would expect, less about that monetary outcome.
zh: 所以我认为驱动我们的东西和你想的一样，不那么关乎金钱回报。

speaker: Unknown
en: And holy shit, we've put ourself in a place to be one of the hopefully leading firms in AI.
zh: 然后天哪，我们已经把自己放在了有望成为 AI 领域领先公司之一的位置上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And how do we really compound and double down on that advantage?
zh: 而我们要如何真正复利这个优势并加倍押注呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's the energy I feel every day, certainly from myself and all my partners.
zh: 这就是我每天感受到的能量，当然来自我自己和我所有的合伙人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I just can't see that going away.
zh: 我实在看不出这会消失。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's kind of like, it's kind of like we arrived, we're here.
zh: 有点像，有点像我们已经到达了，我们就在这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do we do with that?
zh: 我们要拿这个做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And the money's great, but that's not why we did all this.
zh: 钱当然很好，但这不是我们做这一切的原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think richer investors make better investors because you do not worry about downside mitigation, but you focus on upside optimization.
zh: 我认为更富有的投资人会成为更好的投资人，因为你不用担心下行风险的缓解，而是专注于上行空间的优化。

speaker: Unknown
en: How big can this be?
zh: 这个能有多大？

speaker: Unknown
en: What happens if this works?
zh: 如果这个成了会怎么样？

speaker: Unknown
en: You're not worried about LPs not re-upping.
zh: 你不用担心 LP 不续投。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're not focused on risk mitigation.
zh: 你不专注于风险缓解。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you agree with me in thinking that?
zh: 你同意我这个想法吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Of course I do.
zh: 我当然同意。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it's at a firm level and it's at an individual level.
zh: 而且我认为这既在公司层面，也在个人层面。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's been times in my career where you feel some doubt, either from yourself or those around you, and it makes you dramatically worse, right?
zh: 在我的职业生涯中，有过一些时刻你会感到一些怀疑，无论来自你自己还是你周围的人，这会让你急剧变差，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what we try to do is have a high trust environment, build people up, and everyone is going to fail in this business, right?
zh: 所以我们努力做的是营造一个高信任度的环境，给人们建立信心，而在这个行业里每个人都会失败，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just kind of recognizing that sooner and kind of landing the plane or doing the right thing.
zh: 只是更早地认识到这一点，然后让飞机着陆，或者说做正确的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Act like the reality is not the reality.
zh: 表现得好像现实不是现实。

speaker: Unknown
en: And oftentimes you're doing a founder a favor by even helping them kind of land the plane.
zh: 而且很多时候，你甚至是在帮创始人一个忙，帮他们让飞机着陆。

speaker: Unknown
en: So yeah, I think it's an important point and an important thing to manage in this business.
zh: 所以是的，我认为这是一个重要的观点，也是这个行业里需要管理的一件重要事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would love to move into a quickfire round.
zh: 我很想进入快问快答环节。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have pushed and prodded around many different areas, so I appreciate the patience.
zh: 我已经在很多不同的领域里追问和试探过了，所以感谢你的耐心。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is where the really off-putting stuff comes.
zh: 真正让人不舒服的部分来了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm ready.
zh: 我准备好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Dude, you were born ready for this.
zh: 老兄，你生来就为此做好了准备。

speaker: Unknown
en: What have you changed your mind on in the last 12 months?
zh: 在过去 12 个月里，你改变了什么想法？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, certainly just how big companies can be and how bold Menlo should be in pursuing those, that we need people who are free thinkers and willing to take those kind of risks.
zh: 我的意思是，当然，就是关于公司能有多大，以及 Menlo 在追求这些目标时应该有多大胆，我们需要那些自由思考、愿意承担那种风险的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's more true than ever, like just how big a company can be.
zh: 而且这比以往任何时候都更真实，比如一家公司能有多大。

speaker: Unknown
en: Biggest miss and what was your lesson from it?
zh: 最大的错失是什么？你从中学到了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: The things that I would look back on at the time as the biggest miss no longer feel that way.
zh: 当时我会回顾并视为最大错失的那些事情，现在不再有那种感觉了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's like, I'll give you one.
zh: 所以就是说，我给你讲一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, we were at the One Inch Line winning Plaid back in the day, and I have the utmost respect for Zach and the company and what they've done.
zh: 你知道，当年我们在「一英寸线」上争夺拿下 Plaid,我对 Zach 和那家公司以及他们的成就怀有最崇高的敬意。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the point in time, I felt like when I lost that, that that was like existential to my career and ability to win.
zh: 但在那个时候，当我输掉那个的时候，我觉得那对我的职业生涯和获胜能力来说像是生死攸关的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, they're a great company.
